create.name: Douglas Cardwell
create.bio:
Douglas Cardwell is a percussionist and sound bath practitioner in Albuquerque, New Mexico, where he founded Lotus Sound Bath. He studied music education at James Madison University and percussion at Rice University's Shepherd School of Music, then spent three decades playing and teaching, including years as principal timpanist of the New Mexico Philharmonic and concerts in halls across the United States, Germany and Russia. He later trained in sound meditation with Ascending Sounds and in energy work with Jeffery Allen, and designed a mallet for singing bowls and gongs that is now sold by a percussion maker.

His sessions are wordless and instrumental: people lie down while he plays tuned quartz crystal bowls, several symphonic gongs at once, chimes and other instruments, as a way into deep rest and meditation. Once a month, on a Monday evening, he leads a free sound bath in the Cathedral of St. John downtown, seasonal sessions at yoga studios and outdoor venues around the city, and private group sessions in homes and workplaces. Recordings of his sound baths, along with short spoken mindfulness pieces, are free on YouTube and Insight Timer, where he also streams some sessions live.

courses.title: In-Home or On-Site Private Group Sound Bath
courses.description: He brings his bowls, gongs and chimes to your home or venue for a 60-minute sound bath for a private group of four or more, on a date you choose. Booked online.
courses.price: $85 USD per person plus tax (4 person minimum)

courses.title: Workplace Wellness Sound Baths
courses.description: Single sessions or a series of sound baths for staff teams, planned with each organisation around its people and schedule. Past hosts include a radio station and a property management firm.

courses.title: Sunday Sound Bath at Board30
courses.description: A one-hour afternoon sound bath at Board30 on Alameda Boulevard in Albuquerque. Bring a mat or thick blanket, a pillow and something warm.

courses.title: Winter Solstice Sound Bath at Desert Lotus Yoga
courses.description: A seasonal one-hour sound bath marking the solstice at Desert Lotus Yoga in north-east Albuquerque, with a guest musician.

free_resources.title: Douglas Cardwell on Insight Timer
free_resources.description: His recorded sound baths with crystal bowls and gongs, each built around a simple intention, free to hear in the app or on the web, with some sessions streamed live.

free_resources.title: Free Monthly Sound Bath at the Cathedral of St. John
free_resources.description: An hour-long sound bath open to everyone on the first Monday evening of every month at the Cathedral of St. John in downtown Albuquerque. Free with online registration; bring a mat or use the seating.

lotussoundbath.com sits behind a Cloudflare challenge for curl, so site text was read through WebFetch (summaries) and the bio check ran against those extracts, the Acuity booking descriptions and the partial Insight Timer bio.
Socials are business accounts under the Lotus Sound Bath name, all clearly run by him.
Sound bath videos are instrumental; kept as his core practice (not music releases), but a human may treat them as music-only. YouTube has 21.3k subscribers but most videos have a few hundred views.
His business copy calls the work 'sound healing' and a 'therapeutic session'; plan wording keeps to relaxation and meditation.
Two dated public sound baths (15 Nov, 19 Dec 2026) included with dates; they will need removing after they pass. The free monthly series link points at the public-events booking category.
Studio private sessions (7400 Montgomery Blvd NE) are described on the site, but no studio session is currently bookable; only the in-home group option is listed.
